stories.headline: Colorado's 2026 water year was warmest on record by wide margin, state climatologist reports
stories.summary:
The 2026 water year ending September 30 will be the warmest in Colorado history by a significant margin, according to state climatologist Russ Schumacher of the Colorado Climate Center at Colorado State University. The state averaged 5.6 degrees Fahrenheit above the 1971-2000 baseline, with record-warm months including December, February, March and August, as well as the warmest spring and summer ever recorded.

Despite the heat, September rains have offered some relief, particularly in western and southeastern Colorado. Southwestern Colorado has received twice its monthly average rainfall, and Ignacio, near the New Mexico border, recorded a 100-year storm event last week with 2.85 inches of rain in a single day.

Nevertheless, 88% of the state remains in drought, with 44% classified as extreme drought or worse. Long-term drought metrics indicate conditions are the worst ever recorded, slightly exceeding the severe 2002 drought.

Looking ahead, a developing Super El Niño — with greater than a 90% probability of forming — is expected to bring above-average precipitation to most of Colorado over the next 15 days and through early winter, though forecasters caution that its impact on snowfall remains uncertain.

stories.headline: Health insurance premiums on Colorado's individual market to rise 10% in 2027
stories.summary:
Premiums on Colorado's individual health insurance marketplace will increase an average of 10% in 2027, according to the Colorado Division of Insurance. The increase is a significant drop from the 22% average rise seen in the current year, though many Coloradans are already facing higher out-of-pocket costs after pandemic-era federal subsidies expired at the end of 2025.

For residents receiving state financial assistance, the average monthly cost increase will be approximately $20. Without the state assistance Colorado's legislature approved earlier this year, that figure would have been $69 per month. Regional variation is notable, with increases ranging from about 6% on the Eastern Plains to nearly 16% in the Grand Junction area.

Insurers had initially requested an average 11% increase, but regulators approved a lower rate, which the Division of Insurance says will save consumers a combined $42.1 million. Colorado's approved increases are below the national median of 15% that insurers requested across the country.

Colorado's reinsurance program will also reduce premiums by nearly $470 million next year by backstopping insurers against unusually expensive claims. The program allows insurers to lower premiums across the board for all marketplace customers.

stories.headline: Colorado gubernatorial debate dispute: Moderator says Marx campaign confirmed agreement in writing
stories.summary:
A dispute has emerged over whether Republican gubernatorial nominee Victor Marx agreed to a debate with Democratic nominee and Attorney General Phil Weiser moderated by veteran Colorado political commentator Aaron Harber. Marx publicly stated he never agreed to Harber as moderator, but Harber says his team obtained written confirmation from the Marx campaign.

Harber published an email exchange showing that on September 7 he sent a detailed outline of debate terms to Marx campaign staffer Rachael Flick, requesting a thumbs-up if the terms were acceptable. Flick responded the following day with: 'This is our thumbs up.' Harber said he has never in nearly 100 debates seen a campaign disavow a staffer's written confirmation.

Marx posted on Facebook that Harber 'attempted to insert himself as a moderator and change the format,' and that he did not agree to the arrangement. Harber countered that such a claim is implausible given the Marx campaign's small staff size, saying it is hard to believe the candidate was unaware of a confirmed agreement for what would be the campaign's largest media event.

The standoff leaves the status of a formal general election debate between Marx and Weiser unresolved. With Colorado's gubernatorial race competitive, many voters and political observers have expressed interest in seeing the candidates face off before November.

stories.headline: Colorado Springs to get UFL professional football team starting in 2027 season
stories.summary:
The United Football League announced Wednesday that Colorado Springs will join the league as an expansion team beginning in the 2027 season. The team will play home games at Weidner Field, the 8,000-seat downtown stadium currently home to the Colorado Springs Switchbacks FC soccer club.

UFL president and CEO Russ Brandon indicated the team's name, logo and colors will reflect Colorado's outdoor heritage, its identity as an Olympic City, and the strong military presence in the region, anchored by the U.S. Air Force Academy and several major installations. Full branding details are expected to be revealed on October 25.

Weidner Field, which opened in 2021, will become the highest-elevation professional football stadium in the country at 6,035 feet above sea level. The announcement marks the second professional sports franchise at the venue.

Colorado Springs becomes one of the newer markets in the UFL, a spring football league that has been expanding its footprint across the country. The addition gives Colorado two professional football teams, alongside the NFL's Denver Broncos.

stories.headline: Avalanche enter new season as Stanley Cup favorite despite conference final sweep; Bednar awaits contract extension
stories.summary:
The Colorado Avalanche are entering the 2026-27 NHL season as one of the league's top Stanley Cup contenders, according to an Associated Press season preview capsule. Colorado won the Presidents' Trophy last season for the NHL's best regular-season record before being swept in the conference final by the Vegas Golden Knights.

Head coach Jared Bednar, the franchise's all-time wins leader, is entering the final year of his contract without an extension in place, adding an element of uncertainty to an otherwise strong organizational outlook. The team's core remains intact heading into training camp.

Separately, the Avalanche on Tuesday placed defensemen Domenick Fensore and Christian Wolanin on waivers, per a team transaction announcement. The club also faces questions about replacing forward Valeri Nichushkin, who was traded to the Columbus Blue Jackets in a cost-cutting move this offseason.

Colorado's combination of elite talent and organizational depth keeps them among the Western Conference favorites, though the conference final exit after a dominant regular season raised questions about playoff performance that the team will look to answer this year.

stories.headline: Denver Nuggets open training camp with overhauled roster, new approach at backup center behind Jokic
stories.summary:
The Denver Nuggets enter the 2026-27 NBA season with a significantly reshaped roster as training camp opens, following a first-round playoff exit against the Minnesota Timberwolves. The offseason saw the team lose forwards Peyton Watson, Tim Hardaway Jr., and Bruce Brown, as well as backup center Jonas Valanciunas, prompting a philosophical shift in how the front office is building around three-time MVP Nikola Jokic.

Rather than commit $10 million-plus to a starting-caliber backup center as they did last year with Valanciunas, general managers Jon Wallace and Ben Tenzer instead signed Marvin Bagley III at a lower price point. The change reflects a reassessment after Valanciunas posted a minus-27.6 net rating in 25 playoff minutes against Minnesota, erasing much of the regular-season value he had provided.

The Nuggets also added veteran guard DeMar DeRozan, who averaged 18.4 points in 77 games for Sacramento last season, to provide shot creation when Jokic rests. Oddsmakers have set Denver's win total at 49.5, with BetMGM listing the team at +2500 to win the NBA Finals.

Denver native Kieran Cebrian was separately named captain of the University of Denver hockey program for the 2026-27 season. The defending NCAA champion Pioneers will also feature alternate captains Cale Ashcroft, Sam Harris, Jake Fisher and Kyle Chyzowski as the program defends its national title.

stories.headline: Manitou Springs police seek public help one year after Margaret Woolsey disappearance
stories.summary:
The Manitou Springs Police Department is appealing for public assistance one year after 57-year-old Margaret Woolsey was reported missing on September 23, 2025. Investigators say the case remains unsolved and they are hoping renewed public attention will surface new leads.

The MSPD has been working the investigation in coordination with the Colorado Bureau of Investigation, the Colorado Springs Police Department's homeless outreach team, the El Paso County Sheriff's Office and at least one additional agency. No suspect has been publicly identified.

Authorities have not released details about the circumstances surrounding Woolsey's disappearance or where she was last seen. The multi-agency effort reflects the complexity of the case after a full year without resolution.

Anyone with information about Margaret Woolsey's whereabouts or disappearance is encouraged to contact the Manitou Springs Police Department.

stories.headline: Rare tropical bird never before seen in Colorado draws birders to Eastern Plains, helps Littleton resident reach 500-species milestone
stories.summary:
A piratic flycatcher, a migratory bird native to Central and South America, was spotted at Stalker Lake State Wildlife Area on the Eastern Plains this past weekend — the first confirmed sighting of the species in Colorado and the northernmost sighting in United States history. Only 15 confirmed sightings of the piratic flycatcher have ever been recorded in the U.S., with previous sightings concentrated in the Southwest, Florida and Kansas.

The rare bird drew dozens of Front Range birdwatchers who made the drive to the Eastern Plains on short notice. For Littleton resident Joey Kellner, 62, the sighting served as his 500th unique species recorded in Colorado, making him the first person with publicly documented records to reach that milestone. Colorado's full state bird list currently stands at 522 species, soon to be 523 once the piratic flycatcher is formally accepted.

Kellner is a longtime leader of Denver Field Ornithologists birding trips and has led monthly bird walks at Chatfield State Park for 30 years. He previously mentored Chris Wood, now director of the eBird project at Cornell Lab of Ornithology, when Wood was a teenager.

'It's a search for feathered treasure,' Kellner said. 'You never know when you get up in the morning what you're going to see.' Peter Gent, president of Colorado Field Ornithologists, called reaching 500 species 'a significant achievement' given the state list totals only 522 confirmed species.

stories.headline: Purgatory Resort offering $9 lift tickets with $10 resort credit for upcoming Colorado ski season
stories.summary:
Purgatory Resort near Durango is offering lift tickets priced as low as $9 for the 2026-27 ski season, with many of those days also carrying a $10 resort credit — effectively making some ski days free or better. The resort is targeting a November 20 opening day, weather permitting.

Using a dynamic pricing model, tickets are priced below $50 on approximately 95 days throughout the season, representing about 70% of expected operating days. The most expensive single-day lift ticket available is $89, set for Saturday, January 2.

The upcoming season will also mark the debut of the resort's new Colorado Couloir chairlift, opening approximately 40 acres of advanced and expert terrain in one of the mountain's steepest areas. Purgatory spans more than 1,600 acres of skiable terrain, exceeding the size of popular locals' favorite Arapahoe Basin.

The pricing announcement comes as Colorado ski resorts prepare for a season that could benefit from El Niño-driven precipitation. Front Range skiers willing to make the drive to southwestern Colorado can access the deals at Purgatory's website.

stories.headline: Tucker Gulch Trail in Golden closed due to heavy bear activity amid statewide surge in encounters
stories.summary:
The city of Golden has closed Tucker Gulch Trail between 1st Street and 7th Street until further notice due to heavy bear activity in the area. The paved trail runs through a residential neighborhood less than a mile from downtown Golden.

City officials attribute the increased bear presence to drought conditions that have depleted natural food sources, forcing bears to forage closer to developed areas. Golden experienced a separate high-profile bear incident earlier this year when a hiker was attacked by a bear at Apex Park in June.

The closure is the latest in a series of bear-related incidents across Colorado, where statewide human-wildlife encounters have reached record levels this year. Wildlife officials continue to urge residents to secure trash, lock windows and doors, and remove other potential attractants from their properties.

No injuries have been reported in connection with the Tucker Gulch Trail closure. The trail will remain closed until authorities determine the area is safe for public use.

stories.headline: World's Wonder View Tower in Genoa marks 100th anniversary as reimagined art museum, closes for season Saturday
stories.summary:
The World's Wonder View Tower in Genoa, a plains town about 100 miles east of Denver, is celebrating its 100th anniversary and grand reopening as a vertical immersive art museum after years of disrepair. The 65-foot roadside attraction, once famous for its claim that six states are visible from its observation deck, closed in 2013 and was rescued by a local nonprofit for a major restoration.

Four prominent Colorado artists have transformed individual floors of the tower: Phil Bender, Mark Friday, Deborah Jang and Denver-based installation artist Lonnie Hanzon, who created 'The Red Room,' a maximalist immersive space drawing on the tower's original 1960s paint scheme. Hanzon is known locally for projects including Denver's original Parade of Lights, the 'Evolution of the Ball' sculpture outside Coors Field and the Denver Center's annual 'Camp Christmas' experience.

This Saturday, September 26, marks the final day of the 2026 season to visit the tower, with hours from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. followed by a 6 p.m. harvest moon party. Public response to the reopened attraction has been described as enthusiastic.

The reopening is part of broader cultural activity in the region. Opera Colorado separately announced it will open its 2026-27 season with Verdi's 'Macbeth' November 7-15 at the Ellie Caulkins Opera House in Denver, the first season fully programmed by new Artistic Director Barbara Lynne Jamison.

topStory.headline: Trump Signs Greenland Security Deal, Amending 1951 Treaty to Expand U.S. Military Access and Exclude Rivals
topStory.summary:
President Donald Trump signed a new security agreement Tuesday with the prime ministers of Denmark and Greenland on the sidelines of the United Nations, ending months of diplomatic turbulence over the Arctic island territory. The deal amends and supplements a 1951 defense treaty between the United States and Denmark, adding provisions for expanded U.S. military access, two new American bases, and restrictions barring non-NATO countries from establishing a military presence in Greenland.

The two planned bases will be located at Narsarsuaq in southern Greenland — the site of the former American Bluie West One base that closed in the 1950s — and at Mestersvig in eastern Greenland, currently home to Denmark's Sirius Dog Sled Patrol unit. The U.S. military will also gain free access to air, land, and sea routes between the two facilities, and fast-track approval processes will be established for potential drone warfare installations, though Denmark and Greenland retain final authority over where such facilities are built. Greenland already hosts the Pituffik Space Base, where approximately 150 American troops operate a ballistic missile monitoring site.

Defense analysts described the practical military expansion as modest. Mark Cancian, a senior adviser at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, estimated the total troop increase could be fewer than 50 personnel, despite Trump's description of the deal as the beginning of a 'large military presence.' The restrictions on non-NATO nations are widely seen as directed at China and Russia, and the agreement also includes provisions ensuring continued U.S. military access in the event Greenland becomes independent from Denmark — a contingency that had not been addressed in the original treaty.

The deal is a notable departure from early 2025, when Trump threatened to take Greenland by force and imposed tariff threats on European nations that objected. European allies, alarmed by the rhetoric, held discussions about the future of transatlantic security arrangements without U.S. participation. Former Biden administration official Iris Ferguson told CNN the episode caused significant damage to Arctic security cooperation, though she said the new agreement moves toward advancing shared goals.

The agreement still requires ratification by Danish and Greenlandic lawmakers before taking full effect. The deal also references Trump's proposed 'Golden Dome' missile defense system, though that program remains years from completion. Analysts noted that the core framework largely codifies arrangements already permitted under the 1951 treaty, with one significant procedural distinction: Greenland itself is now a named signatory to the agreement.
